title: 250th Anniversary of the Founding of the United States Marine Corps
summary:
The proclamation marks the 250th anniversary of the United States Marine Corps, celebrates its history and service, and designates November 10, 2025, as a national day of commemoration. It honors past battles and sacrifices, highlights the Marines’ role at home and abroad, and announces more than $150 billion in new investments aimed at building a stronger, modern force.

In practical terms, this means a public call to display the flag and hold ceremonies, along with a pledge to support Marines with new spending on ships, missile defense, and advanced technology. The statement leans into themes of strength, readiness, and unwavering support for Marines, invoking iconic moments like Iwo Jima and the Corps’ motto, “Semper Fidelis,” meaning always faithful.

Those who benefit most are Marines, veterans, and their families, who receive national recognition and a promise of better equipment and resources. Military communities and industries tied to defense production may also see gains from the announced spending. Supporters of a robust national defense are likely to welcome the emphasis on readiness and deterrence.

At the same time, some may be concerned about the size and focus of the new investments and what they mean for the federal budget and other priorities. Critics might worry that a more force-first posture could overshadow diplomacy or lead to escalations abroad. Others may question the framing of military policy and whether it signals a shift in how the country positions its armed forces in the world.

Overall, the document is both a tribute and a policy signal: a celebration of Marine heritage paired with a commitment to increased military strength and visibility.
